The one on the top is my favorite - coil spring, and recessed button. The bottom knife is the only double action in the group (it can be opened manually as well as automatically).

Note the variation in the notches at the base of the blade, and in the button position. There are many varieties, probably dozens, including some recent Chinese clones built on fake 110s. Some are very well made by real craftsmen, others, not so much.

These knives have a spotty reputation but I guess I've been lucky, I've been happy with all three of mine. There is a bit of side-to-side play in each of them, you'll notice it if you look for it, but it's not bad. Once open, the backlock is as secure as any 110. The buttons are positive and the opening action is fast and crisp. The coil spring version is especially nice in this regard.

Avoid the ones with a dimple at the base of the blade instead of a notch. These are only held closed by the tip of a pin pressing into the dimple and they can wear out quickly and become dangerous. A recessed button is always nice on any auto knife without a reliable safety, but for some reason this is an uncommon feature on this model.

I have a soft spot for these as I carried a standard 110 for many years, which I'd equipped with an aftermarket, screw-on thumb stud for one-handed opening. I remember thinking how an automatic version would be just about perfect, but back then such a thing was unobtainable. It's nice when you can finally have something that you've wanted for so long, so I might have gone a little overboard in buying three of them.
